svg.data-weight: 2.37 kg (5.22 lb), Table 9; the external AC supply is 2.05 kg (4.52 lb) and the DC supply 1.85 kg (4.07 lb), Table 15
svg.data-poe-budget-w: 240 W with one 340 W supply and 360 W with two (system budget 66 W), Table 29
svg.data-poe-standard: PoE++ (90 W by default) on all 12 ports
svg.data-power-input-ac: 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, to the external 340 W AC supply (Table 26)
svg.data-power-input-dc: 20.4 through 72 VDC at the external 340 W DC supply's terminal block, nominal +24, -48 or -60 VDC (Table 36)
svg.data-cooling: fanless, convection cooled (Table 8); at least 2 in of clearance around the switch except the mounting side
svg.data-operating-temp: -40 to 60 C in a sealed enclosure, -40 to 70 C in a ventilated enclosure (40 LFM) and -40 to 75 C in a blower-equipped enclosure (200 LFM), up to 15000 ft; safety certified at 60 C
svg.data-storage-temp: -40 to 85 C in the shipping container
svg.data-altitude: no performance degradation up to 15000 ft (4572 m)
svg.data-virtual-chassis: up to 10 EX4100, EX4100-F and EX4100-H switches; the two VCP cages are the Virtual Chassis ports (HiGig or HGoE mode) and the two uplink cages support HGoE only. A 10GBASE-T transceiver cannot form a Virtual Chassis in a VCP
svg.data-macsec: the four 2.5 Gbps ports and the two uplink ports are MACsec capable
svg.data-dry-contact-alarm: two alarm inputs (5 V threshold) and one alarm relay output (NO, COM, NC), Table 4
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: the two uplink and two Virtual Chassis cages take 1 Gbps SFP and 10 Gbps SFP+ transceivers; Tables 44 to 53 list the industrial-grade optics against the ambient they allow. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
